item.title: China's Long March legacy through Turkish eyes
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-24
BEIJING/ISTANBUL, Oct. 24 (Xinhua) -- This year marks the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March and the 55th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between China and Türkiye. Turkish scholars, students and political figures say the military odyssey offers insights into China's revolutionary history and development path, while calling for deeper cultural and people-to-people exchanges between the two countries. The Red Army, led by the Communist Party of China (CPC), was mainly made up of soldiers from peasants' and workers' families during the Chinese revolution. Between 1934 and 1936, the army trekked roughly 12,500 kilometers to break through the encirclement of the Kuomintang forces, a journey later known as the Long March. Murat Tamer, a Turkish scholar specializing in cultural exchanges between China and Türkiye, said the Long March deserved greater recognition in Türkiye. More than a historic march, it demonstrated the CPC's determination, organizational strength and strategic thinking in the face of formidable challenges, he said. The great spirit of the Long March, Tamer added, could help Turkish people better understand how China overcame difficulties and forged its own path of development. For Turkish students in China, the Long March also offers lessons that resonate with their own experiences. Berfin Adiyaman, a master's student in applied economics at Northwestern Polytechnical University, said learning about the Long March had deepened her understanding of the importance of perseverance. While studying in China, she has faced challenges including language barriers and homesickness. Her involvement in exchanges between Chinese and Turkish businesses, as well as her work at a logistics company in Xi'an, northwest China, enabled her to gain a closer look at Chinese society, she said. "Whether it is a country or an individual, courage and perseverance are essential in the face of adversity," Adiyaman said, adding that she hoped to contribute to China-Türkiye economic cooperation and youth exchanges. Yuksel Mansur Kilinc, a member of the Türkiye-China Interparliamentary Friendship Group of the Grand National Assembly of Türkiye, said China's development path has attracted attention in Türkiye, particularly its focus on common prosperity, harmony between humanity and nature, and the coordinated development of material and spiritual civilization. Kilinc said China and Türkiye have new opportunities to deepen bilateral ties. Events marking the 55th anniversary of diplomatic relations have been held across Türkiye this year, reflecting interest in expanding exchanges between the two countries. Describing cultural exchanges as an important foundation for bilateral relations, he called for closer cooperation in the media and cultural sectors alongside economic and technological collaboration, saying such efforts could promote mutual understanding and support the long-term development of China-Türkiye relations. ■

item.title: Rescue efforts continue after 7.0-magnitude quake in China's Xizang
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-24
A volunteer makes noodles at a quake-hit village in Maru Township of Baqen County, Nagqu City, southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region, Oct. 24, 2026. As of 11 a.m. Saturday, 52,450 items or sets of disaster relief supplies had been sent to the quake zone, while more than 2,500 rescue personnel were engaged in relief operations. Authorities have established 35 temporary resettlement sites in the disaster zone. Medical treatment and public health and epidemic prevention efforts are proceeding in an orderly manner, according to the local emergency command headquarters. (Xinhua/Tenzin Nyida) LHASA, Oct. 24 (Xinhua) -- Rescue and relief efforts continue after a 7.0-magnitude earthquake struck Baqen County of the city of Nagqu in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region, local authorities said Saturday. The earthquake, which struck at 10:33 p.m. on Thursday, has left 16 people dead and 76 others injured. The quake has also damaged or destroyed 339 homes and 20 livestock sheds. As of 11 a.m. Saturday, all 76 injured people were receiving timely medical treatment, with five of the 11 people initially classified as seriously injured having improved to a mild condition, according to the local emergency command headquarters. Meanwhile, relief supplies and rescue personnel continue to arrive in the affected areas. As of 11 a.m. Saturday, 52,450 items or sets of disaster relief supplies had been sent to the quake zone, while more than 2,500 rescue personnel were engaged in relief operations. The supplies include 4,651 tents, 2,000 prefabricated houses, 11,772 folding beds, 5,715 quilts and other cold-weather necessities. A large Wing Loong unmanned aerial vehicle has also arrived at the site. Authorities have established 35 temporary resettlement sites in the disaster zone. More than 1,600 personnel from Baqen County, 347 firefighters from the Nagqu fire and rescue detachment, and 530 police officers from the Nagqu public security bureau have been deployed, alongside vehicles and search-and-rescue dogs. Medical treatment and public health and epidemic prevention efforts are proceeding in an orderly manner, the headquarters said. As of 2 p.m. Saturday, the headquarters said 949 aftershocks had been recorded in the affected areas, including eight measuring 4.0 to 4.9 in magnitude and 33 measuring 3.0 to 3.9. All temporary speed restrictions on the quake-hit section of the Qinghai-Xizang Railway were lifted on Friday night, according to China Railway Qinghai-Xizang Group Co., Ltd. A comprehensive inspection found no abnormalities, and trains resumed normal operations, the company said. Power supply in the quake-hit area was fully restored on Saturday night, according to the State Grid. State Grid Xizang Electric Power Co., Ltd. urgently dispatched teams to the affected area for emergency power restoration after the quake, the state-owned utility said. More than 300 personnel along with vehicles, power generation facilities and emergency equipment have been deployed as of Saturday to ensure power supply for the on-site command center, provide lighting for resettlement sites and restore damaged power lines. Local authorities said construction on the first batch of prefabricated houses in the quake-affected areas started at around 2 a.m. Saturday. As more units arrive, residents currently staying in tents will gradually move into the better-insulated temporary housing. "We will ensure that affected residents have safe shelter, warm clothing and bedding, hot meals and clean drinking water," said Pan Zhiqing, Party chief of the Nagqu Municipal Emergency Management Bureau. At a hospital in Baqen's neighboring Sog County, many injured residents were sent there for treatment overnight. The hospital has arranged medical treatment and prepared hot meals and daily necessities for patients. Early Friday morning, Norbu Wangchen, a local resident in Sog County, brought more than 100 portions of Tibetan noodles, along with Tibetan tea and tsampa, to the hospital to help those affected by the earthquake. Help also came from the city of Xigaze, some 700 kilometers away from Baqen. Du Guoping, who was preparing to open two new restaurants in Xigaze, postponed the openings after learning of the earthquake and headed to the disaster zone with more than 1,500 kg of dumplings. His team set off at midnight on the night of the earthquake. After a bumpy journey, the team purchased additional supplies, including food containers and bottled water, along the way. After arriving, Du and his staff set up cooking equipment and prepared dumplings for rescue workers and affected residents. They worked during the day, and at night, the six team members squeezed into two vehicles to rest, keeping the heating on to ward off the high-altitude chill. With more than 500 kg of dumplings still remaining, Du said the team planned to stay for at least three days to cook all the food they brought. Watching firefighters, medical personnel and rescue teams race against time at the disaster site left a deep impression on him. "We feel honored to be able to contribute in our own way," he said. ■ Staff members transfer coal for heating at a quake-hit village in Maru Township of Baqen County, Nagqu City, southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region, Oct. 24, 2026. item.title: China hosts global governance forum to pool wisdom for better future
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-24
XIONGAN, Oct. 24 (Xinhua) -- China is hosting a three-day inaugural global governance forum to pool wisdom for better global governance, one year after the country proposed the Global Governance Initiative (GGI). The 2026 Global Governance Forum (Xiongan) opened on Friday in Xiongan New Area, north China's Hebei Province. Hosted by the Chinese People's Institute of Foreign Affairs, it is themed "Rebuilding Confidence and Cooperation: Reforming and Improving Global Governance in a Transforming World." In a message to the forum, Chinese President Xi Jinping noted the world is undergoing accelerated transformation unseen in a century, and the deficits in peace, development, security and governance are growing rather than diminishing. "I have put forward the GGI to promote the building of a more just and equitable global governance system and a better world," he said. China stands ready to work with all parties to uphold the vision of global governance featuring extensive consultation, joint contribution and shared benefits, pool strength through confidence-building and tackle challenges through cooperation, Xi said. He called for efforts to promote the implementation of the GGI to inject more certainty and positive energy into a world of turbulence and transformation, and jointly move toward a community with a shared future for humanity. "The forum offers a window for the world to follow the developments of China's vision for global governance. One of the key points is to invite all countries to communicate together and build a world together and share the outcomes together," said Selcuk Colakoglu, director of the Ankara-based Turkish Center for Asia-Pacific Studies. Nearly 400 representatives from strategic, political, academic, business, media, and youth sectors from more than 90 countries and international and regional organizations, including the UN, attended the event. The GGI emphasizes sovereign equality, international rule of law, multilateralism, a people-centered approach, and practical outcomes, providing an opportunity for all parties to further engage in the global governance system, international cooperation and dialogue, former Nepali President Bidya Devi Bhandari said. The world today faces severe challenges such as economic inequality, poverty, geopolitical tensions, armed conflicts, climate change, and food security, while rising protectionism and unilateralism further complicate international cooperation. No single country can address these shared challenges alone; they require dialogue, enhanced cooperation, and joint efforts among all countries, Bhandari said. Former Kyrgyz Prime Minister Djoomart Otorbaev said countries of the Global South support the GGI and want a world of growth, cooperation and progress instead of hegemony or interference. "Our system is still designed without giving developing countries sufficient weight. So we see the need in the United Nations to make reforms to our governance systems," UN under-secretary-general Guy Ryder said. It is important to enhance the representation and voice of the Global South in international affairs, advance reform of the international financial system in accordance with the timetable and roadmap agreed by all parties, increase the representation of developing countries in the Security Council, and give full play to the important role of emerging multilateral cooperation mechanisms such as BRICS and the Shanghai Cooperation Organization, Chinese foreign minister Wang Yi said. Wang also called for improving governance rules in emerging fields, turning new frontiers such as the deep sea, the polar regions and outer space into areas for international cooperation, and evolving an artificial intelligence (AI) governance structure based on general consensus soon. China and the United States have both the capability and the responsibility to jointly develop and govern AI well, ensuring that its development remains under human control and benefits the people, Wang said when meeting with co-chair of the Board of Trustees of the Asia Society John L. Thornton and The New York Times columnist Thomas L. Friedman on the sidelines of the forum. Thornton and Friedman said that the international community is paying close attention to the upcoming APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting hosted by China, and expects that China will take this opportunity to play a unique and positive role in tackling global challenges. ■

item.title: China voices firm opposition to U.S. proposal to expand outbound investment curbs
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-24
BEIJING, Oct. 24 (Xinhua) -- China on Saturday expressed "grave concern" and "firm opposition" to a recent U.S. Treasury proposal that would expand and intensify restrictions on outbound investment in China, calling it a discriminatory move and a typical practice of overstretching the concept of national security. A spokesperson for China's Ministry of Commerce made the remarks in reply to a media query on the U.S. Treasury's proposed updates to the outbound investment security program, which are open for public comment. The proposed rules "run counter to the important consensus reached by the two heads of state, disrupt normal economic and trade cooperation between Chinese and U.S. enterprises, and undermine the international economic and trade order," the spokesperson said. China will closely follow further developments and reserve the right to take corresponding measures, the spokesperson noted. "U.S. restrictions on investment in China would not only harm China-U.S. economic and trade cooperation but also hurt the interests of U.S. firms," the spokesperson said, noting that investing in China is investing in the future as the country boasts immense consumption and investment potential with its super-large market. China urges the U.S. side to respect market economy principles, stop overstretching the concept of national security, stop politicizing and weaponizing economic and trade issues, and create a sound environment for bilateral economic and trade cooperation, according to the spokesperson. ■

item.title: Xinhua Commentary: Marking Taiwan Recovery Day with shared resolve to advance China's reunification
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-24
BEIJING, Oct. 24 (Xinhua) -- As China prepares to mark the 81st anniversary of its recovery of Taiwan and observe the Taiwan Recovery Day on Oct. 25, the occasion offers an opportunity to revisit a glorious chapter of history, in which people on both sides of the Taiwan Strait jointly resisted foreign aggression, and to draw strength from the past to advance reunification. China's recovery of Taiwan in 1945 was a hard-won victory in the Chinese people's resistance against Japanese aggression during World War II, and a defining moment in the nation's struggle to safeguard its sovereignty and territorial integrity. Starting in 1840, China endured a period of immense suffering amid foreign aggression and the decay of feudal rule. Japan's aggression marked some of the darkest chapters in modern Chinese history. Following its war against China in 1894, Japan seized Taiwan and the Penghu Islands in 1895, subjecting Taiwan to five decades of colonial rule. Faced with both internal turmoil and foreign invasion, the Chinese people valiantly fought against the invaders, ultimately defeating Japanese aggression to safeguard the country's sovereignty and territorial integrity. On Oct. 25, 1945, after China's victory in the War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression and the broader World Anti-Fascist War, Taiwan was recovered. This historic day, forever etched in the history of the Chinese nation, deserves to be remembered by people on both sides of the Strait. Throughout the struggles against foreign aggression and for national liberation, Taiwan shared the fate of its motherland China. Patriots in Taiwan resisted Japanese colonial rule through political, military and cultural struggles, with more than 650,000 giving their lives during the five decades of Japanese occupation. Driven by the conviction that "to save Taiwan, one must first save the motherland," over 50,000 people in Taiwan went across the Strait to join the fight against Japanese aggression, risking their lives to defend the dignity and honor of the Chinese nation. Historical archives and photographs capture the island's jubilant celebrations when China recovered Taiwan in 1945. Families decorated their homes with lanterns, brought out ancestral tablets, and burned incense to share the good news with their forebears. Residents poured spontaneously into streets to cheer, while the sound of firecrackers rang out into the night. These memories, forged through bloodshed and sacrifice, testify to the deep-rooted bonds between people in Taiwan and their fellow Chinese on the mainland, as well as the shared destiny of people on both sides of the Strait. China's recovery of Taiwan was an important outcome of victory in the Chinese People's War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression and the World Anti-Fascist War, and provides compelling evidence that the Chinese government resumed the exercise of sovereignty over Taiwan. The Cairo Declaration, issued in 1943, stipulates that all territories Japan had stolen from China, including Taiwan and the Penghu Islands, shall be restored to China. The Potsdam Proclamation of 1945 reiterates that "the terms of the Cairo Declaration shall be carried out." In September 1945, Japan signed the instrument of surrender, pledging to fulfill the obligations set out in the Potsdam Proclamation. On Oct. 25 that year, the Chinese government announced that it was resuming its exercise of sovereignty over Taiwan. A ceremony to accept Japan's surrender in Taiwan Province of the China war theater of the Allied powers was held in Taipei. From that point forward, China had recovered Taiwan de jure and de facto through a host of documents with international legal effect. Taiwan's status as an inalienable part of the Chinese territory was thereby reaffirmed, and the question of Taiwan's status was resolved. However, an unresolved civil war and foreign interference have left the two sides of the Strait in a prolonged state of political confrontation. The fact that the two sides of the Taiwan Strait have yet to be fully reunified is a scar left by history on the Chinese nation, but the fact that Taiwan is an inalienable part of China's territory has never changed. Driven by their political interests and secessionist agenda, Taiwan's Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) and other secessionist forces have repeatedly claimed that Taiwan's status remains undetermined, distorted historical accounts in textbooks, pursued educational policies that remove Chinese cultural elements, and propagated a separatist narrative in an attempt to sever historical ties across the Strait and mislead younger generations in Taiwan. Since Lai Ching-te took office in 2024, the DPP authorities have conspicuously avoided mentioning China's victory in the War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression and China's recovery of Taiwan. The DPP authorities have also repeatedly downplayed or whitewashed Japan's colonial rule over Taiwan. Such actions betray the fundamental interests of the Chinese nation. Achieving national reunification is a responsibility shared by all Chinese people, including people in Taiwan. The establishment of the Taiwan Recovery Day enables people on both sides of the Strait to commemorate this historic moment together. The Taiwan question originated in a weak and ravaged China, and will be resolved as China achieves national rejuvenation. Commemorating Taiwan's recovery today is an opportunity to draw strength and resolve from the sacrifices of the war and the recovery of lost territory, while reaffirming the determination and confidence to advance national reunification. ■

item.title: China's top political advisor accompanies DPRK top leader on visit to border city
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-24
Wang Huning, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, accompanies Kim Jong Un, general secretary of the Workers' Party of Korea and president of the State Affairs of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK), to visit the Memorial Hall of the War to Resist U.S. Aggression and Aid Korea in Dandong, northeast China's Liaoning Province, Oct. 24, 2026. Wang on Saturday accompanied Kim on a visit to Dandong in northeast China's Liaoning Province and conveyed General Secretary of the CPC Central Committee and Chinese President Xi Jinping's cordial greetings and best wishes to Kim. (Xinhua/Rao Aimin) DANDONG, Liaoning, Oct. 24 (Xinhua) -- China's top political advisor Wang Huning on Saturday accompanied Kim Jong Un, general secretary of the Workers' Party of Korea and president of the State Affairs of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK), on a visit to Dandong in northeast China's Liaoning Province. Wang, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, conveyed General Secretary of the CPC Central Committee and Chinese President Xi Jinping's cordial greetings and best wishes to Kim. On Saturday morning, Wang greeted Kim at the square of the Memorial Hall of the War to Resist U.S. Aggression and Aid Korea and accompanied him to present a flower basket to the memorial tower. The national anthems of China and the DPRK were played, and honor guards laid the flower basket. Kim approached the flower basket and arranged the ribbon, which read, "The martyrs of the Chinese People's Volunteers (CPV) are always remembered." In a solemn atmosphere, all present paid silent tribute to the martyrs. Inside the memorial hall, Kim viewed the historical artifacts showcasing the bravery of the martyrs and the side-by-side fighting of Chinese and DPRK soldiers, and gifted a historical photo bearing his personal inscription to the hall. During their meeting, Wang said on the occasion of the 76th anniversary of the CPV's entry into the DPRK to fight in the War to Resist U.S. Aggression and Aid Korea, General Secretary Kim Jong Un's special trip to Dandong fully demonstrates how much the party and government of the DPRK value the China-DPRK friendship forged with blood. He said the visit is highly significant, as it not only carries forward the traditional friendship between China and the DPRK and consolidates the popular support for friendship, but also deepens political mutual trust and advances cooperation and development. In September last year and June this year, General Secretary Xi Jinping and General Secretary Kim Jong Un made historic mutual visits and reached a series of important common understandings, guiding the traditional friendly and cooperative relations between China and the DPRK into a new historical period, Wang said. China stands ready to work with the DPRK to unswervingly implement the important consensus reached between the top leaders of the two parties and two countries, and take their common socialist cause as a bond to further develop China-DPRK relations, Wang said. The opening of the new China-DPRK Yalu River bridge can be taken as an opportunity to expand personnel exchanges and trade cooperation and better benefit the two peoples, he said. He called for strengthening strategic communication and collaboration to foster a peaceful and stable external environment for safeguarding their respective sovereignty, security and development. Kim asked Wang to convey his cordial greetings and best wishes to General Secretary Xi Jinping, and wished the upcoming fifth plenary session of the 20th Central Committee of the CPC success. Kim said that he has come to Dandong on this special trip to pay tribute to the martyrs of the CPV, who sacrificed their lives to support the DPRK at a critical historical juncture, and to express the DPRK's heartfelt gratitude and eternal respect for these heroes. General Secretary Xi Jinping's historic visit to the DPRK in June this year demonstrates the high importance attached to DPRK-China relations and marks a milestone in the development of bilateral ties, Kim said. Noting that this year marks the 65th anniversary of the signing of the DPRK-China Treaty of Friendship, Cooperation and Mutual Assistance, Kim thanked China for its long-term support and assistance to the DPRK's socialist cause, and said the prospects for cooperation between the two sides are very broad. The DPRK admires the remarkable development achievements scored by the Chinese people and their rightful important international standing under the leadership of General Secretary Xi Jinping, Kim said, adding the DPRK stands ready to work with China to carry forward historical friendship, expand practical cooperation, and bring tangible benefits to the people of both countries. In the afternoon, Wang accompanied Kim to visit a car factory in Dandong, where they inspected the production workshop and heard a briefing. When Kim left Dandong, Wang saw him off at the new China-DPRK Yalu River bridge. ■ Wang Huning, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, accompanies Kim Jong Un, general secretary of the Workers' Party of Korea and president of the State Affairs of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK), to present a flower basket to the memorial tower at the square of the Memorial Hall of the War to Resist U.S. Aggression and Aid Korea, in Dandong, northeast China's Liaoning Province, Oct. 24, 2026. item.title: Interview: Xi's vision for global governance responds to changing world, says Tajik expert
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-24
DUSHANBE, Oct. 24 (Xinhua) -- The Global Governance Initiative (GGI) proposed by Chinese President Xi Jinping reflects the objective transformation of the world system and responds to the aspirations of most countries for a more just and equitable system of global governance, said Rahmon Ulmasov, a professor at the Russian-Tajik (Slavonic) University. In a recent interview with Xinhua, Ulmasov described the initiative as one of China's most significant initiatives in recent years, saying it came at a time when the existing global governance system was facing serious challenges. "Geopolitical conflicts, sanctions and trade wars are intensifying, while the gap between developed and developing countries is widening. At the same time, existing international institutions are becoming increasingly inadequate in addressing global problems," Ulmasov said. Against this backdrop, he said, reforming and improving global governance has become increasingly important to ensure that international institutions can better respond to emerging challenges and reflect the interests and concerns of countries around the world. Ulmasov noted that the GGI builds on China's previously proposed Global Development Initiative, Global Security Initiative and Global Civilization Initiative. "Together, they form a coherent Chinese vision for international development, based on the interconnection between development, security, dialogue among civilizations and the improvement of global governance," he said. He stressed that global governance should be based on equality among countries and decision-making through consultation, which is in line with the core principles of the GGI. In his view, effective global governance also requires countries with different political systems, civilizational traditions and national interests to strengthen dialogue and seek common ground while respecting their differences. "The ability to build cooperation despite differences is one of the most important elements of modern multilateral governance," Ulmasov added.■

item.title: Xiplomacy: Xi's remarks on upholding authority, role of UN
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-24
BEIJING, Oct. 24 (Xinhua) -- Saturday marks United Nations Day, commemorating the anniversary of the UN Charter's entry into force in 1945. On multiple occasions in recent years, Chinese President Xi Jinping has reiterated China's support for the international system with the United Nations at its core, and called for upholding the authority of the United Nations, practicing true multilateralism, and observing the purposes and principles of the UN Charter. The following are some highlights of his remarks. Sept. 13, 2026 At the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, India, Xi said all countries, regardless of their size, strength or wealth, are equal members of the international community. "Global South countries should hold high the banner of multilateralism, uphold the authority and role of the United Nations, support multilateral institutions in advancing reform and increasing efficiency, and ensure the equal participation of all countries in international affairs," he said. July 17, 2026 At the opening ceremony of the 2026 World AI Conference and High-Level Meeting on Global AI Governance held in Shanghai, Xi said that AI is an invaluable asset that encapsulates humanity's collective wisdom. "We should practice true multilateralism and recognize the important role of the United Nations," he said. "We should enhance alignment and coordination on AI development strategies, governance rules and technical standards, so as to form a consensus-based global governance framework at an early date to make this frontier technology better benefit humanity." Sept. 1, 2025 At the "Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Plus" Meeting in north China's port city of Tianjin, Xi said the purposes and principles of the UN Charter and other universally recognized basic norms of international relations must be observed comprehensively, fully and in their entirety. "We should firmly safeguard the status and authority of the United Nations, and ensure its irreplaceable, key role in global governance," he said. Aug. 30, 2025 When meeting with UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres on the sidelines of the SCO Summit 2025, Xi said that China will always be a trustworthy partner of the United Nations. China is willing to deepen cooperation with the United Nations, support the United Nations in playing a central role in international affairs, and jointly shoulder the responsibility of safeguarding world peace and promoting development and prosperity, Xi told Guterres. June. 28, 2024 At the conference marking the 70th anniversary of the Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence held in Beijing, Xi said that in the face of new developments and challenges, "the authority and central role of the United Nations can only be strengthened rather than weakened." "The purposes and principles of the UN Charter are never outdated, and they are getting ever more important," he said. "China advocates the vision of global governance featuring extensive consultation and joint contribution for shared benefit, and China believes in true multilateralism." ■
